rows.title: The First Bout

incomingChoices.text: Walk to the arena floor.
Go before the thunder lands. First move, no ceremony.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You cross the chalk before the bell's echo dies, and the crowd loves you instantly, at least until the next odds shift. The scout catches your first strike an inch from his jaw and grins. Somewhere above the rim, thunder answers the bell, one beat early.

incomingChoices.text: Circle him. Watch the feet, not the hands.
incomingChoices.conclusion: His hands lie twice before his feet tell you the truth: the weight sits back before every real strike. On the third exchange, the shift starts again. You move before his hands finish lying, and his grin disappears. At the rail, Mira murmurs that nobody watches feet their first night.

incomingChoices.text: Tell the clerk to raise the purse first.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The crowd howls with delight at the nerve of it, and the odds swing hard while the clerk chalks a fatter line. Win or lose, you just taught the whole rim your name. The board, notably, spells it right this time.

rows.title: The Captain's Line

incomingChoices.text: Stand over the wounded man. He is not walking, and he is not booked.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You plant yourself between the stretcher and the line. The Captain glances at the square, then at the guards who would have to drag you away in front of it. incomingChoices.text: Challenge the Captain, by name, in the open square.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The oldest law in Stormveil: a posted challenge outranks a booking. The crowd chalks it on the nearest wall before the clerk can even arrive. The Captain takes off his cloak, folds it, and says he was hoping somebody would do this, and the square becomes an arena, because here it always was one.

incomingChoices.text: Hold up the tallied order. Ask, loudly, who counts riots before they happen.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The square goes still. The Captain reads the route lines, the wax, the tally marks, and for one long moment he is a man looking at his own orders and not liking their handwriting. 'Booking stands,' he says. He folds the order into his own coat, then signals the arrest himself.

incomingChoices.conclusion: Mira yells your name and misses your collar by a finger. You go over the pipework at the banked crystal with your hands bare, and the whole floor howls awake at once. Whatever happens next, the engine will remember tonight the way a body remembers a burn.

rows.title: The Grove Trial

incomingChoices.text: Follow Mori to the grove.
Bow low to the roots first, and mean it.
incomingChoices.conclusion: Mori raises his eyebrows. The Guardian rises out of the soil slowly, almost politely, like an old keeper getting up to greet a guest.

incomingChoices.text: Watch the Guardian's pattern before you move.
incomingChoices.conclusion: It circles the way roots grow, in slow spirals that repeat. By the second pass you know where the next root will break the soil. Behind you, Mori stops reciting instructions and counts the spiral under his breath. The Guardian turns inward toward you.

incomingChoices.text: Strike first. Show the grove what's growing.
incomingChoices.conclusion: Toma makes a sound like a kettle boiling over. The Guardian catches your first blow and the whole yard shakes, and somewhere under the soil, something old starts paying attention.

rows.title: Did You Give, Or Did You Take

incomingChoices.text: Face the Sentinel.
Douse the nearest rack line and see what happens.
incomingChoices.conclusion: Steam screams up the flue and half the chamber's warmth dies at once. Far above, faint through the stone, you hear the village notice the cold. The Sentinel moves toward you, and for one strange moment it seems to approve.

incomingChoices.text: Count the stamps. Every household. Every season.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You reach forty one households before the Sentinel closes the distance. Forty one, in this season alone. Mori watches you count, and every rack seems to age him another year.

incomingChoices.text: Demand Mori say who signs the approvals.
incomingChoices.conclusion: 'One hand,' he says, not looking away from the fire. 'The same hand for thirty years.' The Sentinel hears the answer too, and its grief sharpens into something with edges.

Take the oath and rise.
Rise as Jonin.
Fight carefully. Give the watchers nothing to write down.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You give the first exchange no flourish and no wasted motion. Hoshina tilts her head. 'Restraint,' she tells the hall, 'grafts well.' The old Master hears her and sets his feet. Hoshina watches both of you with the same appraising stillness.

incomingChoices.text: Fight as yourself, whatever it shows them.
incomingChoices.conclusion: Your opening is loud, untidy, and entirely yours. The old Master catches the blow, then laughs like the sound surprised him. Above the trial floor, the black flower on the Register glows brighter. He waves you in again before Hoshina can call the exchange.

incomingChoices.text: End it fast. Break the Master's stance in three moves.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The first break comes in three moves. The hall gasps. Up close, the old Master's face shows relief before discipline shuts it away. He rebuilds his stance around the grafted roots. Retirement is not among the choices the Register gave him.

incomingChoices.text: Scatter the crates into the dark. Burn the wagon and manifest.

incomingChoices.conclusion: You and Toma drag two crates under the road roots and fold the manifest inside his coat. The retrieval squad finds four crates still lashed to the wagon and counts six spaces. Their leader looks from the empty bindings to the ash on your sleeves, then orders a search before either hidden crate can be carried clear.

incomingChoices.conclusion: Toma takes the wagon into the trees while you remain in the road. The retrieval squad spreads across it, listening to the wheels fade behind you. Their leader asks where he went. You give no answer, and the first rank draws before Toma is safely out of hearing.

rows.title: Grief, Off the Chain

incomingChoices.text: Say the founders' words to it: 'given gladly.' Mean them.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The words land on it like rain on a roof it used to live under. For three heartbeats the Beast is just forty ordinary dead people remembering gladness, and then it fights you the way grieving people fight: to be held, not to win.

incomingChoices.text: Shatter the chain. Whatever follows, follows.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The chain parts with a sound like a hymn ending. Freed grief takes the shortest road toward what hurt it, and the shortest road runs through you. Far above, in her tower, the keeper feels her bellows die.

incomingChoices.text: Ask the Avatar what it hasn't told you. Then fight.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The Avatar admits the founders' gifts protected the village for only two winters each generation. incomingChoices.text: Bind the Rootfire to willing gifts alone. Sheathe the shears forever.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The fire shrinks to the founders' flame. Every unsigned stamp splits, and from tonight the Rootfire accepts only willing adult signatures. The lower seam opens, finds nothing it is allowed to take, and closes. Ashen Leaf will have to ask for its warmth now, winter by winter. Hoshina bows to the new rule. The fire in her does not.

battle.bossName: Kage Hoshina Enju, First Flame Vessel

incomingChoices.text: Take the shears. The village needs a keeper who was never fooled.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You take the shears and claim Hoshina's authority. The Register had been steering your assignments toward this role, hoping you might replace her. The pipe to Hollow Gate remains open, and the control ledger lists you as the next person authorized to approve a cut. Hoshina accepts your challenge and attacks to decide who keeps control.

rows.title: The Alpha Guard

incomingChoices.text: The Alpha Guard bars the hall.
Break the rows out now. All forty-three, whatever it costs.
incomingChoices.conclusion: Forty volunteers take your signal and put hooks to the first frozen row. The White Silence Guard steps between them and the release wheel. Breaking all forty-three free will drain the vault by afternoon, but none of that happens unless you move the thing guarding the lever now.

incomingChoices.text: Post yourself at the rows. Nobody freezes, nobody vanishes, on your watch.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You take the post in front of the frozen rows and call the first name. A villager answers for the person who cannot. Another voice answers the second. The White Silence Guard steps into the roll and raises its weapon. Keeping all forty-three visible starts with holding this post.

incomingChoices.text: Map the rows against the vault's intake schedule. Find the payment date.
incomingChoices.conclusion: Forty-three names, forty-three seal dates, and the vault's draw curve from Sova's meter converge three weeks out. The vault is short, and Kael is using the White Silence to cover the payment date. The Guard crosses the figures with one pale arm before you can copy the final column.

incomingChoices.text: Face him at the meter.
He turns back to the meter.
He sets the letter down like a sleeping child.
She sets the book on the meter.
Enough. The Count ends here.

Outside, struck names answer Yura's roll by choice. Kael hears them and attacks before the release can finish. Surviving the next winter will still require watch crews, fuel, and shelter freely supplied.

incomingChoices.text: Bind the vault. Metered, lawful, every struck name a case with your signature.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: The yard is silent because it is built silent: sand raked to swallow footsteps, walls hung with cloth that eats echoes. Whatever happens here happens unheard.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Narrator
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: There is no bell. There is no instructor. There is a woman on the canal steps who sold you the truth for free, watching from the wall with interest that isn't entirely professional.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Narrator
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: No one is coming. That's the test. That was always the test.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Narrator

rows.title: The Bookmaker's Confession

incomingChoices.text: Tell him exactly what you saw. Seams, drain, direction of flow.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You give it to him like a rigger's report, plain and orderly, and the old man takes out a purse ledger and writes it down in the margin, the first non-number he has entered in forty years. 'There,' he says, shaky. 'Witnessed. That's how it starts, apparently.'

incomingChoices.text: Say nothing yet. Chalk the seam lines where they glowed.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You walk the cooling sand and chalk every line while Vanta watches, and the pattern is unmistakable once drawn: eleven channels, one drain, dead center. A diagram of a mouth. You copy it small onto your own slate, and now the count exists somewhere the floor can't drink it.

incomingChoices.text: Post a grudge of your own and watch the floor while you fight it.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You post a small but genuine grievance and fight at the next bell. During the bout, you feel the floor trying to weaken your connection to that reason. incomingChoices.conclusion: Forty ryo, receipt issued, your name off her client's page and into your own pocket. She stamps the transfer with visible satisfaction: clean trades are her love language. rows.title: The Windows Light

incomingChoices.text: Climb in the open at first dark, the lit windows at your back.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You approach the tower openly while returned files and names remain displayed in windows across the canal. Iro serves his signed confession on the watch desk, and three officers refuse an anonymous order to clear the road. The rest stand aside. Nyx follows with her evidence, and the shrine witness waits below to begin reading the names after the confrontation.

incomingChoices.text: Climb with the case: receipts, manifest, and Iro's unsealed third draft.
incomingChoices.conclusion: You go up as a proceeding, not a spectacle: the sealed returns, the buyer's traced chain, and a profiteer's four-in-the-morning confession, carried by the one shinobi on the canal every faction will let pass. The lit windows hold the market below. The paper climbs. In Moonshadow, a sealed record has always cut deeper than an open blade.

incomingChoices.text: Send word up first: the discrepancy is coming, and it has read its own file.
incomingChoices.conclusion: The message reaches the tower before you do: the person they could never price has read the file. Several Veiled Hands remove their seals or refuse the next anonymous order. At the top of the tower, Sable begins moving papers from one stack to another. Nyx reads the same message over your shoulder. 'She is afraid,' she says. 'Good. So am I.'

rows.title: Your Own No

incomingChoices.text: Refuse tonight's meal and wait at the seam
incomingChoices.conclusion: At dusk the seam parts on a slate of names, each beside the one thing its owner refused to cede. You read until the light goes and set it back. As the seam closes, a glyph surfaces beside your hand: the same cut that marks older acts of refusal, not a name or a Bloodline sign. Serel checks it against her staff. 'Same cut. Somebody saw you say no.'

incomingChoices.text: Measure the stone, copy its rule, touch nothing
incomingChoices.conclusion: You sketch the ring, the seam, the cold sun side, and write the rule beneath: opens for a refusal, witnessed. Serel corrects your moss line by a handspan and walks you back to the road.

incomingChoices.text: Drive a chisel into the seam and pry
incomingChoices.conclusion: By the third strike the seam is gone and the stone is one smooth piece. You cairn the spot for a return with better tools, and Serel shoulders her pack without a word.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Emissary Corvane
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: A Legacy is not an ancestor coming back, and it is not something sleeping in a Bloodline. In the Sunken Court's age, people later called the Withheld refused to cede one defining choice.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Emissary Corvane
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: What survived was the shape of the choice. Across old accounts, witnesses kept recognizing the same hundred patterns: mercy, calculation, ambition, endurance. A Legacy returns when someone freely repeats one under witness.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Emissary Corvane
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Isa's descendants do not own one. But this family has repeated her disputed act for generations. Which pattern they teach depends on which account is true, and her name is missing from all three.

incomingChoices.text: Break the seal with her and split the penalty
incomingChoices.conclusion: Inside are clay tallies stamped with living names and RECEIVED IN FULL. Beneath them lies an older slab. rows.title: The Book Stays Open

rows.title: Nailed to the Board

incomingChoices.text: "We split a penalty once and you nailed the manifest up for anyone to read. This is that, bigger."
incomingChoices.conclusion: She remembers the crate. Most people who split a penalty with her spend the rest of their lives pretending they did not. She writes your name in the readers' column of a book she does not usually show anyone.

incomingChoices.text: "You owed me a favor on the books, no expiry. Call this it paid."
incomingChoices.conclusion: She opens the ledger to the line she wrote, favor owed, your name spelled right, and draws one clean stroke through it. Paid, she says, and looks almost sorry to close the account.

incomingChoices.text: "Last time I turned you in for the fee. I'd rather have done this instead."
incomingChoices.conclusion: She does not pretend she forgot the two hundred. She wrote something short in her ledger that day, and shows you it now: worth watching. She adds a second line under it. Watched.

incomingChoices.text: "Read the whole scheme out at every village at once. No favors, no seats spared."
incomingChoices.conclusion: She sends the manifest to all four waystation boards on the same night, every seat named and every buyer priced. When the courier asks which copy is hers, Harrow says, 'None. Keep moving.'

actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: The rations ran short in the third year. Not evenly short. The hill wards kept their full measure, and the kiln wards starved by a fifth.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Let us dispose of the mystery early. I knew. From Lyra's third report onward, I knew what the Gate was drawing, and from whom.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: People imagine a chancellor deceived by his ministers. I was the best-informed man in the Court. Every floor below you crossed this desk as a number.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Turn the Gate off, and by the fourth day the pumps stop, and the high cisterns hold three days of water. The cold stores fail, and half a winter's food spoils in a week. The healing wards go dark with four hundred people inside them.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Every one of those figures was real. I checked each one twice because I wanted one of them to be false.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: In the first winter, shutting it down meant a thousand dead within days. Keeping it on meant tremors, missing names, and sick workers spread across the city. I chose the harm that did not arrive all at once. Then I made the same choice for eleven years.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Understand what the days cost, though. Each one needed quiet, and quiet needed work.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: A dry aqueduct filed as maintenance. A grain ledger adjusted. An engineer discredited, an arbiter leaned on, a district sealed by its own captain's hands. None of it felt like ruin. It felt like the morning's memoranda.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Each day I postponed the shutdown, one more pump, storehouse, or ward came to depend on the Gate. An order made quickly for the sake of a clean conscience would still have left those people without water, food, or light.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Here is the confession, then. Mind, it is not the one people expect.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: There was never a day when shutting it down looked merciful. In the first winter I saw a thousand immediate deaths on one side and smaller harms scattered across the city on the other. I chose what I could explain at the next council meeting.

rows.title: The Verdict

physicalPresence.stagingEvidence: The chamber, the windows full of a city that stopped

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: Do not write that the Gate destroyed us in a night. Nothing so honest. It dimmed us for a generation while we called the dimming necessary.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: It drank the strong, dried the channels, starved the kilns, sealed the gates, bought the tables, and set neighbor against neighbor over grain. And at every step it offered the same bargain. One more day. We took that bargain every single time, and I signed for it.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: I had eleven years to order a shutdown. Each year the cost was higher, and each year I used that as my reason to wait. You have seen what I did.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: It drank the strong, dried the channels, starved the kilns, sealed the gates, bought the tables, and set neighbor against neighbor over grain. And at every step it offered the same bargain. One more day. We took that bargain every single time, and I signed for it.

actionPropEmotionEvidence.speaker: Halden
actionPropEmotionEvidence.text: I had eleven years to order a shutdown. Each year the cost was higher, and each year I used that as my reason to wait. You have seen what I did.
